channel: epbs/_threads/Is it possible to call `on_block()` multiple times with the same block_
searchText: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/874767108809031740/1476264920847876106 here is a similar discussion but around `on_payload_attestation_message` and looks like we never got to the bottom of this cc. <@363800010518822915> Interesting finding! I think at least at the spec level `on_block` should be idempotent, i.e. regardless of a number of calls with the same block the outcome should remain the same. In client this can be preserved by not calling `on_block` for an already processed block. Another way of achieving that would be an early quite from `on_block` when the block is already in the store. I can't see any cons here As noted already in the first message by <@1035747431461167125>. Block -> PTC Attestation -> Block != Block -> PTC Attestation. So while idempotent, it does not commute with adding PTC attestations so the ordering will matter anyway. also it's not strictly idempotent because of `record_block_timeliness`

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
Interesting finding! I think at least at the spec level `on_block` should be idempotent, i.e. regardless of a number of calls with the same block the outcome should remain the same. In client this can be preserved by not calling `on_block` for an already processed block.

Another way of achieving that would be an early quite from `on_block` when the block is already in the store. I can't see any cons here
